reference.method: damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

global.statement: With both coefficients free, every nonempty count sample has an attained maximum. If positives occur it is unique, with $\hat p=1/\bar x_+$ and $\hat p_0$ the empirical zero fraction, where $\bar x_+$ is the positive sample mean. All-zero data give $p_0=1$ and leave $p$ unidentified. Holding either coefficient preserves attainment for compatible data. A free $p_0$ is unique, and a free $p$ is unique exactly when positives occur. Holding all coefficients leaves likelihood evaluation. Held $p_0=0$ excludes zeros, held $p_0=1$ excludes positives, and held $p=1$ permits positive counts only at one.
global.reason: The likelihood factors into a Bernoulli zero-indicator likelihood and the positive geometric likelihood. For $k>0$ positive observations the latter is $p^k(1-p)^{\sum_{x_i>0}(x_i-1)}$, uniquely maximized at $p=k/\sum_{x_i>0}x_i$. This includes the attained endpoint $p=1$ when all positives are one. The Bernoulli factor is uniquely maximized at the empirical zero fraction. Without positives the likelihood is independent of $p$.
